scope: KaoPu Engine function-provider dependency declarations and exact result reuse
problem: A Mother/provider can omit a transitive input while the Engine still forms a stable key from the declared subset. An input Proxy catches only mediated state reads; a provider created in the host realm can retain undeclared closure/global authority and produce a different result under the same declared key.
falsifiableHypothesis: Executed-path read auditing detects hidden dependencies only on mediated channels. If provider source is created or evaluated in a realm whose endowments are limited to the declared dependency set, an undeclared ambient read fails before result publication; passing an already-created host function into that realm does not remove its closure authority.

activation.rollbackPoint: Keep current trusted-provider registration and mark closure/global dependency completeness UNKNOWN if one bounded source-evaluated provider trial is incompatible with required Engine imports, GPU/device objects, or performance. Do not add SES or change production cache behavior in this audition.

teacher.name: Bazel sandboxing and hermetic action model
teacher.specificNovelty: Turn an undeclared input access into an execution failure by exposing only declared inputs, rather than treating a declaration or cache-key equality as proof of completeness.
teacher.boundary: Bazel's default sandbox documentation says host files may remain readable by absolute path; stronger hermetic isolation or a mediated provider access facade is required. Dynamic read observation covers only executed paths.
teacher.integrationDecision: LEARN_PRINCIPLE_NOT_DEPENDENCY; do not add Bazel to KaoPu Engine.

teacherFollowup.name: Endo SES Compartments
teacherFollowup.specificNovelty: Authority is fixed at provider creation/evaluation: a compartment can start without ambient authority and receive explicit endowments, but moving an existing host function into a compartment does not erase its captured closure.
teacherFollowup.boundary: Endo warns that the host must maintain the boundary and harden endowments; the project remains under active security review. Current KaoPu providers are trusted module functions with imports and closures, so direct integration has unmeasured compatibility and performance cost.
teacherFollowup.integrationDecision: LEARN_CONSTRUCTION_BOUNDARY_NOT_DEPENDENCY; do not add SES to KaoPu Engine without a one-provider compatibility trial.

evidenceIncrements.boundedQuestion: How can KaoPu Engine discover a Mother/provider dependency omitted from an exact-reuse declaration?
Can an input read-set audit discover provider dependencies captured through a host closure or global, and where must restriction occur?
